          Premier League Match Predictions: The Opta Supercomputer's Picks for This Week
        
      
                          
                      Oct 22, 2026
          
                      Chloe Horswill / Author, Harry Carr / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
With the help of the Opta supercomputer, we provide our Premier League match predictions for Matchday 8 of the 2026-27 season.
The Opta supercomputer has delivered its match predictions ahead of the latest weekend of the 2026-27 Premier League season, with the table taking shape.

With seven wins from seven, Manchester City sit top of the Premier League table and are the only team left in the competition yet to lose a game this term after their 3-2 win over Ipswich Town last Saturday.

Everton were beaten by Chelsea, and Brentford suffered a late loss to Liverpool as their unbeaten starts came to an end, while there were also first wins of the campaign for Fulham, Bournemouth and Tottenham.
Reigning champions Arsenal edged past Nottingham Forest to stay three points behind City, and Brighton continue to impress after their 5-0 thrashing of Crystal Palace.
But who can make moves up the table this weekend? Matchday 8 sees fixtures take place across Friday, Saturday and Sunday in a bumper weekend.
Ahead of what should be another exciting group of Premier League fixtures, let's check out the Opta supercomputer's match predictions.
The action begins at Portman Road on Friday, as Ipswich Town and Nottingham Forest both aim to get back to winning ways.

Forest have lost their last three Premier League games, more than they had in their previous 14 (W5 D7 L2), and have drawn a blank in four different matches this season, including last time out against Arsenal.

Ipswich won their first two Premier League games against Forest in the 1992-93 season, but they have since lost all four against them, though our predictive model suggests they will end that run, with a 43.2% win probability.

Forest, who have a 30.1% chance of victory, won 4-2 on their last visit to Ipswich in 2024-25, but have not won on consecutive league visits since 2010-11 and 2011-12 in the Championship. At 26.7%, this is one of the most likely draws of the weekend, though, so a stalemate could be on the cards.

Onto Saturday, and Aston Villa will be the next team to try and end Manchester City’s perfect start, after Enzo Maresca made history last weekend by becoming the first manager to win his first seven Premier League games in charge of a club.

City could become the eighth side to win each of their first eight games of an English top-flight season, after Everton in 1894-95 (first eight), Sheffield United in 1903-04 (eight), Tottenham in 1960-61 (11), Manchester United in 1985-86 (10), Liverpool in 1990-91 (eight), Chelsea in 2005-06 (nine), and Liverpool in 2019-20 (eight).
And with a 43.2% win probability, they are the most likely away winners of the weekend.

However, City – who thrashed AEK Athens 5-1 in the UEFA Champions League in midweek – have lost their last two league games against Villa, last losing three straight to them between August 1962 and September 1966.

Villa, whose win probability sits at 31.6%, are unbeaten in their last three home league games against sides starting top of the table (W2 D1), while they are in good form, having won two of their last three league games (D1) and beaten Viking 3-1 in the Champions League.
Arsenal will be waiting to pounce on any potential Man City slip-up, so they’ll be determined to walk away with three points against Everton.

The Gunners, who battled back to draw 2-2 with Bayern Munich in the Champions League on Wednesday, won 69.6% of the supercomputer’s simulations and are the most likely winners of the weekend. They are also unbeaten in their last seven league matches against Everton (W5 D2).

Arsenal have won 11 of their last 12 Premier League games (L1), winning all six at the Emirates Stadium in that run, while their defensive record continues to impress; no side has conceded fewer league goals than them (5), while they’ve also faced fewer shots on target (21) and have a lower xGA figure (5.6) than any other side.
Everton were beaten 2-0 by Chelsea last time out to end their unbeaten start, and are winless in their last eight away league games (D5 L3), with all three on the road this season ending level.
